children: Stock index futures were lower on Tuesday after a strong rally in technology stocks pushed the Nasdaq higher in the previous session.
Here are the five news items investors should watch:
White House launches Trump TV:
The White House launched a 24/7 YouTube livestream called “Trump TV” on Monday, with its inaugural

featuring President Trump speaking at Mount Rushmore. The launch follows the administration’s recent decision to bar journalists from CNN, Politico and MS NOW, and gives investors another channel for monitoring White House messaging and policy developments.
BASF explores Evonik deal:
BASF
has held discussions with Evonik
about a potential transaction this year, Dealreporter reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. One source said the prospects
uncertain, with BASF facing cash constraints and prioritizing the planned Agricultural Solutions IPO before pursuing an acquisition.
Iambic files for IPO:
AI-driven drug discovery company Iambic Therapeutics filed for a U.S. IPO and plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker IAM. Backed by Nvidia
, the San Diego-based biotech plans to use proceeds and existing cash to advance three cancer drug
, while Renaissance Capital estimated the proposed offering could raise up to $100 million.
SpaceX ends shared Falcon 9 missions:
SpaceX

has stopped selling Falcon 9 missions that carry multiple companies, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Some companies have reportedly struggled to secure flights beyond 2028 as SpaceX prepares to wind down its flagship rocket, adding pressure on satellite operators amid delays affecting competing launch vehicles.
Trump administration proposes $5B Middle East energy fund: The

Trump administration has proposed a $5 billion fund to help Middle Eastern countries rebuild energy infrastructure damaged during the Iran war and reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz, The Wall Street Journal reported. The proposal is being discussed with countries including Saudi Arabia and the U.A.E., with the effort highlighting the disruption to regional energy infrastructure and global oil and gas flows.
